related_questions.question: How to create a fire evacuation map for free?

text_blocks.snippet: To create a fire evacuation map for free, you can utilize online tools like RoomSketcher or EdrawMax, or free software like MyDraw. Start by selecting a template or creating a floor plan from scratch, then customize it with evacuation symbols, exit routes, and key features.
Here's a step-by-step guide using online tools:

list.title: 1. Choose a tool:
list.snippet: Select a free online tool like RoomSketcher, EdrawMax, or Evacuation-Planner.com. These offer free versions or trials with basic functionalities.

list.title: 2. Create or import a floor plan:
list.snippet: If you have a floor plan, import it or draw one from scratch using the tool's features. Start with walls, doors, and windows, then add fixed installations.

list.title: 3. Add evacuation symbols:
list.snippet: Use the tool's library to add symbols for emergency exits, fire extinguishers, alarm pull stations, and assembly points.

list.title: 4. Customize and label:
list.snippet: Adjust the size, placement, and orientation of elements. Add labels and exit routes for clarity.

list.title: 5. Review and finalize:
list.snippet: Ensure all elements are accurate and clearly visible. Check for obstructions in evacuation paths.

list.title: 6. Export and share:
list.snippet: Export the map in a suitable format (like PDF or JPG) and print it for display.
All exit doors and stairwells: Clearly mark all exits and routes to them.
Emergency equipment: Show the location of fire extinguishers, first aid kits, and other relevant equipment.
Assembly points: Indicate the designated assembly area outside the building.
Compass and street names: Add a compass arrow and street names for context, especially for areas outside the building.
Labels and annotations: Use labels and text to clarify specific locations and routes.
Clear and well-lit exit routes: Ensure that the routes are easily visible and unobstructed.
Contact information: Include relevant contact information for reporting emergencies.
Written procedures: If required, include written procedures for evacuation.

related_questions.question: How to set up a fire evacuation plan?

text_blocks.snippet: To make a fire evacuation plan, start by mapping your home, identifying two escape routes from each room, and choosing a safe meeting place outside. Practice the plan with everyone in the household, including children, and ensure smoke alarms are functional.
snippet_highlighted_words: start by mapping your home, identifying two escape routes from each room, and choosing a safe meeting place outside

list.snippet: Draw a floor plan of your home, including all doors, windows, and hallways.
Mark two escape routes from each room, including windows and doors.
Consider alternative escape routes, such as fire ladders for upper-story windows, according to Ready.gov.
Select a safe, outdoor meeting place away from your home, like a specific tree, mailbox, or neighbor's house.
Ensure everyone knows where to meet after evacuating.
Conduct regular fire drills, including at night, to familiarize everyone with the plan.
Practice getting low and moving to your exits, as smoke can rise.
Test smoke alarms during drills, suggests gov.je.

list.title: Children:
list.snippet: Plan for how to assist young children and ensure they understand the escape routes.

list.title: Accessibility:
list.snippet: If anyone has mobility issues, plan for their specific needs and ensure exits are accessible.

list.title: Accessibility:
list.snippet: Keep pathways clear of obstacles.

list.title: Security Features:
list.snippet: Ensure any security bars on windows or doors have quick-release mechanisms, according to Mass.gov.

list.title: Smoke Alarms:
list.snippet: Ensure smoke alarms are functional and tested regularly, according to NFPA.

list.title: Document the Plan:
list.snippet: Write down the plan and share it with everyone in the household, posting it near a phone.
